candidate.answerReason: For x>0, the work equation reduces to (x+3)(x−10)=0. Since x+3 is positive, x=10; the six-day contributions are 6/10 and 6/15, whose sum is 1.

methods.label: Clear denominators and extract a common factor
methods.explanation:
In 6 days, A completes \(6/x\) of the project and B completes \(6/(x+5)\). Their contributions add to one project, so, with \(x>0\), set up the equation \(\frac{6}{x}+\frac{6}{x+5}=1\). Both denominators are positive. Clearing the denominators and rearranging gives \(x^2-7x-30=0\).

Splitting \(-7x=-10x+3x\) exposes a common factor:
\[
x(x-10)+3(x-10)=(x+3)(x-10)=0.
\]
Since \(x+3>0\), dividing by \(x+3\) gives \(x=10\). Checking, \(\frac{6}{10}+\frac{6}{15}=1\), so \(x=10\) days.
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 8 polynomial expansion and common-factor extraction. Positivity justifies division by x+3.

methods.label: Check a candidate and prove uniqueness
methods.explanation:
A shorter solo completion time means more work completed in the same six days. For \(x>0\), the combined six-day contribution is \(\frac{6}{x}+\frac{6}{x+5}\). At \(x=10\),
\[
\frac{6}{10}+\frac{6}{15}=\frac{3}{5}+\frac{2}{5}=1,
\]
so 10 days works.

If \(0<x<10\), both denominators are smaller than 10 and 15 respectively, so both contributions are larger and their sum exceeds 1. If \(x>10\), both contributions are smaller and their sum is less than 1. These cases exhaust all other positive values, so \(x=10\) days is the unique answer.
methods.levelReason: Uses positive fractions with equal numerators and elementary inequality comparisons; no function theory is required.
